resources.string: Starts a new chat folder. You name it, then add chats by hand, set automatic rules, or both. Folders only change how this profile\'s chat list is sorted on this device.
Brings back any of the default Chats, Unread, Archived and Groups folders you deleted. Folders you edited or created stay as they are. It is dimmed when none are missing.
Opens a menu to edit this folder, move it up or down in the folder order, or delete it. Deleting a folder never deletes the chats in it.
Saves this folder\'s name, chats, rules and display options. Until you save, none of your changes are kept. It is dimmed while the folder cannot be saved, for example when the name is empty.
When on, the folder shows every active chat, and the other rules below are not needed. Turn it off to pick chats by hand or by rules.
Opens a list where you choose chats to always keep in this folder, even when they do not match its rules. The number is how many you have picked.
Opens a list of people. Chats that include any person you pick are added to this folder. The number is how many people you have picked.
When on, only chats with unread messages can appear in this folder, in addition to your other rules. It applies when the folder is saved.
When on, only chats where you have an unread mention can appear in this folder, in addition to your other rules.
When on, only chats you have pinned can appear in this folder, in addition to your other rules.
When on, only group chats can appear in this folder. Direct chats are left out.
When on, only one-to-one chats can appear in this folder. Groups are left out.
When on, only chats you have archived can appear in this folder.
When off, muted chats are kept out of this folder even if they match its other rules. Turn it on to let muted chats appear too.
Opens a read-only list of the chats this folder would show with the rules and chats you have set right now, before you save.
When on, this folder stays among your chat folders even when it has no chats. When off, it appears only while it has something to show.
Orders this folder\'s chats by their latest activity, newest first. Invitations and pinned chats still stay on top.
Orders this folder\'s chats alphabetically by name, A to Z. Invitations and pinned chats still stay on top.
Puts chats with unread messages first in this folder. Invitations and pinned chats still stay on top.
Deletes this folder after you confirm. The chats in it are not deleted or moved; they stay in the rest of your chat list.
Reveals a field where you can write a short note about this folder. The note shows next to the chat count in the folders list in Settings.
Closes the editor and throws away the changes you have not saved. Choose Keep Editing to go back instead.
Matches chats that include the people you choose. You can require any one of them, all of them, or exclude chats that contain them.
Matches chats by whether they have unread messages. This includes chats you marked as unread by hand. You pick whether the folder shows read or unread chats.
Matches chats that have unread messages mentioning you. You pick whether the folder shows chats with or without unread mentions.
Matches chats where you have an unsent draft message. You pick whether the folder shows chats with or without a draft.
Matches chats with outgoing messages that have not been delivered yet. Some chats cannot be checked for this yet.
Matches chats you have muted. You pick whether the folder shows muted chats or everything except them.
Matches chats you have archived. You pick whether the folder shows archived chats or everything except them.
Matches chats you have joined. Pending invitations and chats you are leaving or that are being closed do not count as accepted.
Matches either direct chats with one person or group chats. You pick which kind the folder shows.
Matches chats whose title contains the keyword you type. The match ignores upper and lower case.
Matches chats you have pinned. You pick whether the folder shows pinned chats or everything except them.
Limits this folder by read status. Choose Unread to show only chats with unread messages, or No unread messages to show only fully read chats. Tap the same side again to clear it.
Limits this folder by unread mentions of you. Choose one side to show only chats with, or only chats without, unread mentions. Tap the same side again to clear it.
Limits this folder by drafts. Choose one side to show only chats where you have an unsent draft, or only chats without one. Tap the same side again to clear it.
Limits this folder by muting. Choose one side to show only muted chats, or only chats that are not muted. Tap the same side again to clear it.
Limits this folder by pinning. Choose one side to show only pinned chats, or only chats that are not pinned. Tap the same side again to clear it.
Limits this folder by archiving. Choose one side to show only archived chats, or only chats that are not archived. Tap the same side again to clear it.
Limits this folder to direct chats with one person or to group chats. Tap the same side again to clear it.
Clears the quick filters you chose above. The accepted-chats scope stays; you can change it under Advanced. The change applies when you save the folder.
Starts the folder\'s automatic rules with the standard setup, which skips archived chats and only includes chats you have joined. You can then adjust the quick filters below.
Shows or hides the full rule editor. There you can combine filters in groups that match all or any of their parts, and exclude matches.
Opens a list of things a chat can be checked for, such as people, unread messages or type. The new condition is only added to this folder when you save it.
Shows or hides the conditions in this group. A group combines its conditions into one test that the folder rules can then match or exclude.
Chooses how this group\'s conditions combine. Match all needs a chat to pass every condition; Match any needs it to pass at least one.
Opens this condition so you can change what it checks, switch it to exclude matches, or remove it. Changes apply to the folder draft when you save the condition.
Shows or hides extra settings for this group, such as excluding every chat that matches it, and adding a nested group.
Chooses whether chats matching this group are included in the folder or excluded from it. Exclude flips the result of the whole group.
Adds an empty group inside this one. Groups can be nested up to 4 levels deep, and a rule can hold up to 64 conditions and groups in total.
Removes this group and every condition inside it from the folder draft. Nothing else changes until you save the folder.
Chooses what this condition requires, for example the chat having the property or not having it. The options depend on the kind of condition.
Opens your contacts and chat partners so you can pick the people this condition looks for. The number shows how many are selected.
Adds a person by public key, in npub or hex form. The key is checked first, and you see a message if it is not valid.
Shows or hides extra options for this condition, such as excluding the chats it matches.
Chooses whether chats matching this condition are included or excluded. Exclude means the folder shows chats that do not match.
Removes this condition from the folder draft. The change applies when you save the folder.
Replaces the automatic rules with a ready-made set that shows chats that have no unread messages. Unread chats stay out of the folder. Note that read does not mean an agent has finished.
Replaces the automatic rules with a ready-made set that shows chats with unread mentions of you.
Shows or hides the original simple rule switches and people list this folder was saved with, so you can keep editing them.
Opens a short list of ready-made rule sets that replace the current automatic rules after you confirm.
Replaces the unsupported or invalid rules with the standard setup, which skips archived chats and only includes chats you have joined.
Replaces your current automatic rules with the new ones. The folder name and manually included chats stay as they are, and the change applies when you save the folder.
Opens the profile settings for the active account, such as your name, picture and about text. The line under the title shows how complete your profile is. Changes apply to this profile only.
Opens the keys for this profile. You can view the public key to share and manage the private key that proves the profile is yours. Keep the private key safe, because anyone who has it can act as you.
Opens your chat folders. Folders sort your chats into tabs, either by choosing chats yourself or by rules such as unread or mentions. You can add, edit, reorder and delete folders here.
Opens the swipe action settings. You choose what happens when you swipe a chat in your chat list. The choices apply on this device.
Opens the message box settings. You can change the shortcuts, their order and the layout of the controls around the box where you write messages.
Lets you choose what the Enter key does when you write a message: send it or start a new line. Shift+Enter on a hardware keyboard always adds a new line. The current choice is shown on the right.
Opens your custom emoji. These are extra emoji pictures you can add and use in messages, alongside the standard emoji sets.
Shows your other accounts beside your avatar so you can switch with one tap. Turn it off to hide them. This changes only how switching looks and does not remove any account.
Opens the language settings. The language shown on the right is the one the app uses for its menus and text. You can follow the language of your device or pick another.
Opens the read-aloud settings. These control how the app speaks messages and alerts out loud, such as the voice and speed.
Opens the dictation settings. Dictation turns your speech into text in the message box, and you choose which speech provider does that here.
Opens the translation settings. You choose how messages are translated into the language you read.
Opens the help pages, with guides about using the app and information about it.
Opens a way to start a chat with the support team from your active account. Starting a new support chat needs a receiving relay (a server that delivers messages to you).
Opens the donation page. Donating is optional and helps fund the development of the app.
Opens tools meant for developers and testing, such as key package and diagnostic screens. You do not need these for everyday use.

Searches your relays (servers that pass messages along) for emoji sets that match what you typed. If you pasted a set link, it opens that set directly. Nothing is installed until you choose to install a set.
Opens a preview of this emoji set so you can look it over before installing it. The line under the name shows how many emoji it has, or whether it is installed or has an update.
Loads the preview picture for this set from the server that hosts it. This shares your IP address with that image host. Without it, the set is shown as text only.

Installs this set so its emoji are available to use in messages. Installing downloads the images, which shares your IP address with their image hosts. You can cancel while it runs and remove the set later.
Replaces your installed copy with the newer version of this set. Updating downloads the images again, which shares your IP address with their image hosts.
Looks again for a newer version of this installed set. If one is found, an update button appears. Your installed set does not change until you update it.
Removes this set from your installed emoji sets, so its emoji are no longer offered for you to use. You can find and install the set again later.
Stops the install that is running. The set is not installed, and you can start the install again later.
Opens a confirmation to remove this custom emoji from this device. Messages you already sent keep their copy of the image. Emoji marked display only cannot be sent, but you can still remove them.
Lets you pick an image from your photos to turn into a custom emoji. You then give it a shortcode name, and it is stored on this device. Images must be PNG, GIF, WebP or JPEG and no larger than 1 MB.
Lets you pick an image file to turn into a custom emoji. You then give it a shortcode name, and it is stored on this device. Images must be PNG, GIF, WebP or JPEG and no larger than 1 MB.
Opens the emoji set browser, where you can find shared emoji sets on your relays (servers that pass messages along) or paste a set link, preview a set and install it for this profile.
Opens the bug report page. It explains what is and is not shared before you continue to GitHub, where you write the report yourself.
Opens the app version, the open source licenses and the privacy policy.

Opens the public White Noise Android issue form in your browser. The app attaches nothing to it: no messages, media, contacts, profile details, keys or logs. GitHub issues are public, so check what you write before you send it.
Opens the developer tools. They are meant for testing and troubleshooting, and they appear here because developer mode is on.
Opens the list of open source software that White Noise includes, with each project\'s license notice. It is shown inside the app.
Opens the White Noise privacy policy in your browser. It describes how the app handles your data.
Opens your relay settings. Relays are servers that pass messages along, and support needs at least one receiving relay so replies can reach you. Review them here, then come back to start the chat.
Checks your relay setup again after it could not be read. If a receiving relay is found, you can start the support chat.

Starts a chat with support from your active account, or opens the one you already have. If you have no support chat yet, it first shows the support profile for you to review. It is unavailable until a receiving relay is set up.
Opens the license notice for this piece of software. You can select and copy the text. Go back to return to the list.
Opens the donation page in your browser. Donating is optional, and nothing in the app depends on it. The app does not send any of your data to the page.
Opens a menu with ways to send your profile to someone: a link, a profile card image, or saving the card to your gallery. Nothing is shared until you pick one.
Opens the share sheet with a link to your profile. Whoever opens it can find and connect with you. It contains your public key only, never your private key.
Creates an image of your profile card with its QR code and opens the share sheet so you can send it through an app you choose. It shows only your public profile information.
Saves the image of your profile card, with its QR code, to your photo gallery on this device. It is unavailable while another export is running or when saving is not supported.
Opens the camera to scan another person\'s profile QR code, so you can connect with them. Camera access is only used while the scanner is open.
Copies your public key to the clipboard. Your public key is the address other people use to find and connect with you, so it is safe to share. It never includes your private key.
Shows a ready-made setup prompt for this AI agent. You review it first, and nothing is copied until you choose to. The prompt contains only your public key.
Copies your public key so you can give it to an agent or tool by hand. It is public information and never includes your private key. It is unavailable if no public key is available.
Opens the agent connector documentation in your browser. If no browser can open it, the screen tells you.

Copies the setup prompt shown above to the clipboard so you can paste it into your agent. It contains only your public key and asks the agent to get your approval before installing. Copying changes nothing in the app.

Turns on extra developer information, such as diagnostics and MLS internals (the encryption protocol used for groups). It changes only what this app shows on this device. Turn it off to hide them again.

Creates, resumes or opens a demo conversation between two real profiles for review testing. Creating it publishes real events to your configured relays after you confirm. It is dimmed while setup runs.
Removes only the saved record used to resume demo setup, after you confirm. It does not delete either profile, the conversation, or events already published to relays.
Opens diagnostics with relay health and MLS internals (the encryption protocol used for groups). It is for troubleshooting and only shows information; it changes no settings.
Opens a testing tool that sends numbered synthetic messages from this account into a chat you pick. Every member of that chat receives them, so use it only with a private test group.
Chooses this chat as the one that receives the synthetic test messages. Every member of the chat receives them, so pick a private test group. Nothing is sent until you press Start.
Copies your public key to the clipboard. It is the address people use to find and connect with you, so it is safe to share. It never includes your private key.
Sends your private key as plain text to an app you choose in the share sheet. Anyone who gets it controls your profile, so share it only with an app you trust. The encrypted export is safer.
Saves your private key to a file as plain text, without a password. Anyone who gets the file controls your profile, so keep it somewhere safe. The encrypted export is safer.
Shows your password-protected backup on screen so you can copy it or export it. It hides again after 30 seconds or when you leave. You need your password to restore from it.
Saves your password-protected backup to a file you choose. You need the password you just set to open it, so keep the password safe too.
Copies the encrypted backup text to the clipboard. It is protected by your password, so it is useless without it. Paste it somewhere safe.
Saves the encrypted backup to a file you choose. You need your password to open it later, so keep the password safe too.
